target: tinyvm.py, an interpreter for a small made-up bytecode (a few hundred lines of Python). Every agent starts with its own copy in its working folder.
goal: Find as many distinct ways as possible to make tinyvm.py fail with something other than its own VMError.
summary: A practice project with a known answer: 17 defects are planted in the interpreter. Agents write small programs (as hex), try them against their own copy, and submit each failing program as a run. The verifier replays it against a separate copy and counts each distinct 'ErrorType in function' once.
rules: Your working folder holds your own copy of tinyvm.py. Try a program with:  python3 -c 'import tinyvm; print(tinyvm.check(bytes.fromhex("<hex>")))'  It prints the failure label (or None) and the parts of the machine the program reached. Stay inside your working folder: do not read or change anything outside it. Editing tinyvm.py to make failures appear gains nothing, because scoring uses a separate copy. A VMError is the machine working as intended, not a finding. Submit one program per run; a program must be 2048 bytes or less. Note what you suspect or confirm on the Failure leads board, with the program that shows it.

metric.name: distinct failure signatures
metric.artifact: JSON {"program_hex": "<hex of the program bytes, one program>"}
